name: Hanan
title: Levite and temple servant
summary: Hanan is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament, referring to different individuals. The most prominent Hanan is associated with temple service after the return from exile in Babylon. He is mentioned among those who helped the people understand the Law and who sealed their covenant with God under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Hanan among the interpreters of the Law
keyEvents.description: Hanan was among the Levites who helped the people understand God's Law when Ezra read it aloud to the assembly.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Hanan was among those who sealed the written covenant to follow God's Law under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Hanan as steward over the storehouses
keyEvents.description: A man named Hanan, son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, was appointed to manage the temple storehouses because he was considered trustworthy.

keyEvents.title: Hanan mentioned in David's genealogy
keyEvents.description: A Hanan is mentioned as the son of Asael in 1 Chronicles, among David's mighty men and genealogies.

keyEvents.title: Hanan as a temple servant in Jeremiah's time
keyEvents.description: Hanan, the son of Jigdalja, a man of God, had a chamber in the temple where the prophet Jeremiah met the Rechabites.
